correctness.rationale: Exact Gaussian Gram normalization is checked by direct integration and independent Poisson-versus-theta computations. The Jacobi triple product gives strict log concavity in the cosine frequency, reducing the global minimum to endpoints. Strict normalized monotonicity either side of their unique crossing proves the global all-real minimax and reciprocal uniqueness. A uniform nome expansion proves the sharp \(4q^2\) asymptotic. All 145 supporting numerical checks passed, but no infinity claim is inferred from them.

value.rationale: Nearest-neighbor filtering is the smallest nontrivial finite-stencil basis change preserving the canonical Gaussian shift-invariant space. The theorem gives a explicit, width-dependent exact coefficient, proves its global uniqueness up to reciprocal scaling, identifies spectral equality endpoints/interior worst frequency, and shows a quantitatively sharp improvement from \(O(e^{-\pi s/2})\) to \(O(e^{-\pi s})\) in squared Riesz-condition-number excess. This is a natural stabilization benchmark without asserting general multi-tap optimality.
